classification.difficultyReason: Discover an unsignposted SAS similarity from the product equality, transfer its angle relationship to a second triangle pair and convert that similarity into the required product.

content.prompt: $P$ is a point inside triangle $ABC$. $BP$ is extended to cut $AC$ at $Q$ and $CP$ is extended to cut $AB$ at $R$. If $BP\times PQ=CP\times PR$, prove that $AR\times AB=AQ\times AC$.

answer.short:
$AR\times AB=AQ\times AC$.

First prove $\triangle RPB\sim\triangle QPC$ by SAS, then $\triangle ABQ\sim\triangle ACR$ by equal angles.
answer.worked:
The given equality gives
$$\begin{align*}BP\times PQ&=CP\times PR\\\frac{BP}{CP}&=\frac{PR}{PQ}.\end{align*}$$
Also, $\angle BPR=\angle CPQ$ (vertically opposite angles). Therefore $\triangle RPB\sim\triangle QPC$ (SAS).

Hence $\angle PBR=\angle PCQ$ (corresponding angles). Since $A,R,B$ are collinear, $B,P,Q$ are collinear, $A,Q,C$ are collinear and $C,P,R$ are collinear, this gives $\angle ABQ=\angle ACR$.

Also, $\angle BAQ=\angle CAR$ (the same angle at $A$). Thus $\triangle ABQ\sim\triangle ACR$ (AAA), so
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AR}{AQ}&=\frac{AC}{AB}\\AR\times AB&=AQ\times AC.\end{align*}$$
